panels.title: FAK Ops | Fleet Work in Flight & Agent Attribution
panels.description:
Work that has not landed yet (by state and by worktree), and which harness / router model provider / lane each agent run used, how long it worked, how much of that was productive, and the public-vs-private ticket split.

**Honesty contract.** Each plane carries a `*_present` gauge. `0` means the plane is UNAVAILABLE (check `fak_ops_partial` and the `/status` diagnostics) - never a measured zero. An absent ledger folds as present-with-zero-rows. `productive` time is **DERIVED**, not observed: wall time of a run that landed a commit or made a tool call (see `fak_ops_agent_productive_definition`). The gap between wall and productive is suspected-idle time, shown deliberately.

panels.title: Unlanded total
panels.description: Total volume of unlanded work: worktrees whose census state is COMMITTED_UNLANDED, DIRTY_AND_UNLANDED, or ORPHAN_UNREGISTERED_WITH_UNLANDED_COMMIT. ALWAYS read this with the Census present / Census partial stats beside it: a partial census classifies unprobed rows UNKNOWN, so an unlanded total of 0 under census_partial=1 means "not observed", NOT "nothing outstanding".

panels.title: Dirty (not unlanded)

panels.title: Baked top-10 ratios (precomputed by the exporter)
Top-10 share by dimension
panels.description: BAKED top-N concentration: the exporter precomputes each ranked item's share of its dimension total, so this board shows top-10 concentration WITHOUT a PromQL topk()/sum() rewrite at query time. Each bar is one (dimension, rank) pair; the legend reads `dimension #rank`. A rank beyond `fak_ops_top_items_considered` does not exist (see Top-N considered vs truncated), and a missing series means the dimension held fewer items than that rank - not a zero share.

panels.title: Top-10 items (rank, item, value, share)
panels.description: The baked top-N fold, joined into one row per (dimension, rank). `item` is the identity series `fak_ops_top_item` (legend `dimension/rank`, label `item`); `value` is the observed value, `share` the item's share of its dimension total, and `cumulative` the Pareto walk through this rank (at rank 10 it is the top-10 concentration). Rank joined with dimension is the join key, so ranks from different dimensions are never merged. A dimension with fewer items than 10 simply ends early - see `items_considered`.

panels.title: Top-N considered vs truncated
panels.description: `fak_ops_top_items_considered` is how many items the dimension actually held BEFORE the baked top-N truncation. Read it beside the rank axis: a value above 10 means the top-10 bars/rows are TRUNCATED (the dimension held more than shown); a value of 10 or less means the board shows every item, so a missing rank is real absence, not truncation. The gauge carries no `rank` label by design - it is the denominator of the fold.

panels.title: Rank definition in force
panels.description: The BAKED ranking rule the exporter applied, as a one-hot info gauge (`fak_ops_top_rank_definition`, label `rule`). A change here means the ranking is no longer comparable across time - re-read every ratio panel in this row as a different measurement, not a movement.

panels.title: Baked top-N fold present
panels.description: 1 when at least one `fak_ops_top_ratio` series was folded, 0 otherwise. This is the CONFESSION gauge for the whole row: every ratio panel above renders zero when the fold is unreadable, so an empty row and a genuinely flat top-10 look identical unless this says 1.

panels.title: Baked top-N truncated dimensions
panels.description: 1 = this dimension held more items than the baked top-N depth (10), so its ranking is a TRUNCATED view and its cumulative share is a LOWER BOUND on concentration; 0 = the board shows every item in the dimension. Truncation is expected on a busy fleet - it is a scope disclosure, not a fault.
